headline: Options to fund Salem Skipper presented: 5% motor vehicle excise surcharge, 10-cent ride charge, higher parking rates
summary: The presentation estimated the Skipper would cost about $400,000 a year more after the current nine-month period. Its estimates were: the 5% excise surcharge, about $267,000 a year; the 10-cent ride charge, potentially $84,000 a year; and a 50-cent hourly surcharge on about 370 downtown metered spaces, a little over $255,000. Parking rate changes can start sooner because they do not need state approval, while the home rule petitions do. A vote to receive and file the presentation carried.
decisions: Approved receiving and filing the Skipper funding presentation, 4 in favor.
discussion: Funding if petitions fail: Members asked whether the Skipper would continue if the home rule petitions do not pass. The presentation said staff want funding that does not use the general fund or raise property taxes.

Visitor fares: The presentation estimated a higher non-resident rate could save maybe $24,000, $25,000. Staff would identify visitors as people who download the app during busy season and use it once.
Salem State funding: Salem State has not said it would fund the program. Salem State riders make up 13 to 15 percent of ridership, and talks are ongoing.
Parking hours and enforcement: Members asked whether paid parking could run past 6 p.m. The presentation said extending it may need added enforcement, and the numbers are still being worked out.
Contract procurement: The contract came from a request for proposals, not a lowest-bid process. VIA was among the more expensive bidders, but service continuity was the top priority.

decision_evidence.quote: Council historic makes a motion that we receive and file the presentation from Mr. Kuczarski, seconded by Councilor King. All those in favor? See four hands, including my own. The matter carries.
